items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the author theorem at source lines 1213-1216: the power set of the natural numbers is not enumerable. The author proof (1218-1229) carries the diagonal idea without an array: given an arbitrary list of subsets of the natural numbers it defines the set D of those n that are absent from the n-th listed subset, observes D is a subset of the natural numbers, and shows D differs from every listed subset at the point n. The definition of D and the membership flip that separates D from each N_n are the load-bearing steps, so the unit is a real construction rather than a definition unpacking.
